Outbox.native_batch_bounded.detail: The nonempty outbox satisfies both byte/frame caps and the retry size bound. Applying the production batch theorem bounds the length-prefixed native payload by 2*sockCap+maxFrame+4*(2*sockFrames+1). A one-byte cap is explicitly rejected. Closed kernel fixture uses the actual Outbox operations with a local urgent frame, protected handshake, ordinary backlog and reserved retry. Native transport and per-session admission are separate; this is not a whole-app delivery theorem.

Outbox.retry_next_batch.detail: The admitted retry is in the very next batch while local urgent output remains first and ordinary sync is present. No quiet period or ordinary-queue capacity is assumed. Closed kernel fixture uses the actual Outbox operations with a local urgent frame, protected handshake, ordinary backlog and reserved retry. Native transport and per-session admission are separate; this is not a whole-app delivery theorem.

Outbox.push_preserves_reserved.detail: A normal batch overflowing a zero-byte ordinary cap cannot erase the already queued retry or protected control; the actual push returns without closing this transport. Closed kernel fixture uses the actual Outbox operations with a local urgent frame, protected handshake, ordinary backlog and reserved retry. Native transport and per-session admission are separate; this is not a whole-app delivery theorem.

take_append.detail: Nonempty local-write and ordinary-sync queues construct the byte/frame capacity premises; the lane bound also constructs actual admission reachability from empty. The certificate applies the named theorem. Lanes.take and Reserved.offer are supporting component operations; the production Outbox uses Reserved.take and RetrySlot.offer. This is a finite kernel fixture, not native delivery or whole-app convergence.
